data.title: Binance Restores Withdrawals on 87 Networks, Targets Remaining Networks and Assets
data.description: Binance announced on X that it restored withdrawal services on 87 networks this week and aims to resume withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets before the end of next week.

data.title: South Korean Government Says GPU Supply Under Signed Contracts Will Be Unaffected by Jensen Huang’s Resignation
data.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation has raised concerns in South Korea’s AI industry about GPU supplies and AI infrastructure partnerships. According to Odaily, the South Korean government said supplies covered by existing contracts are expected to be unaffected by the management change; about 13,100 Nvidia B200 GPUs have been deployed, and plans to bring in next-generation GPUs, including Vera Rubin, are expected to proceed as scheduled.

Nvidia has partnerships with Naver, Hyundai Motor Group, SK Telecom and Kakao Mobility in areas including AI data centers, autonomous driving and robotics. Market observers believe existing contracts are unlikely to be affected in the short term, while the pace and priority of future investment, technical support and strategic cooperation will depend on decisions by Nvidia’s new management.

data.title: BNB Chain Seeks Feedback on Requirements for Its New L1

data.title: JackYi: Jensen Huang's Return and U.S. Stock Pessimism Cloud Short-Term Dip Buying
data.description:
Liquid Capital founder JackYi said cryptocurrency markets fell on Saturday amid the Jensen Huang event and expectations of a decline in U.S. stocks, adding that a further 30% drop in U.S. equities would not be unusual. According to Foresight News, he said investors should not rush to call a bottom while the situation remains unclear.

JackYi said that after Bitcoin pulled back from $86,000, he had identified $79,000, $75,000, and $71,000 as key levels and bought as the price moved above $77,000. He said Bitcoin’s structure suggested potential for a substantial rebound, but he took profits and sold most of his holdings as U.S. stocks plunged, keeping a small amount of spot Bitcoin.

He said the market’s direction now depends on U.S. stocks and that he is very pessimistic about Jensen Huang’s return and the outlook for equities. As a result, he is not optimistic about short-term dip buying.

data.title: Yi Lihua: No Short-Term Plans to Buy the Dip, Cautions Jensen Huang Event May Keep Pressuring U.S. Stocks
data.description:
Liquid Capital founder Yi Lihua said he is not considering buying the dip in the short term and cautioned that the Jensen Huang event may continue to pressure U.S. stocks. According to Odaily, he said the crypto market continued to fall on Saturday, mainly because of the event, and that expectations for the U.S. stock market had turned pessimistic. A further 30% decline in U.S. stocks was possible, he said, adding that it was too early to conclude the market had bottomed before the situation became clearer.

Yi said he had previously identified $79,000, $75,000 and $71,000 as key support levels for Bitcoin after its pullback from $86,000, and bought the dip near $77,000. At the time, Bitcoin’s own price action suggested significant potential for a rebound, he said. But after U.S. stocks plunged, he took profits and exited in time, retaining only a small spot position.

Yi said crypto market movements are now highly dependent on U.S. stocks. Given his pessimistic view of developments related to the Jensen Huang event and the outlook for U.S. equities, he plans to wait for the situation in the U.S. stock market to become clearer before considering buying the dip.

data.title: Tom Lee Signs Petition Supporting Jensen Huang as Signatures Top 30,000
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said he signed the “Stand with Jensen” petition in support of Jensen Huang. The website lists more than 30,000 signatures, including 2,502 people identifying themselves as current Nvidia employees, 352 as former employees and 17,619 as shareholders. Signers provide their own identities, which the website does not verify.

data.title: Arthur Hayes: FLOP Mining Revenue Depends on Agent Demand for Hardware-Compatible Models
data.description: Arthur Hayes said users on the FLOP network can mine with any hardware, with earnings depending on whether agent demand is for models their hardware can run. According to Foresight News, Hayes shared the remarks in a post on X.

data.title: Ethereum Foundation Transfers 7.79 Million USDS to Multisignature Safe Wallet
data.description: The Ethereum Foundation transferred 7.79 million USDS to a multisignature Safe wallet in the past hour. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens reported that the foundation exchanged 1,000 ETH for about $1.9 million in USDS through CoWSwap. Over the past four days, it has sold 5,000 ETH for about 9.92 million USDS.

data.title: Sky Community Proposes Core Vaults Parameter Changes
data.description: The Sky community has proposed changing Core Vaults parameters, including setting the debt ceilings for ETH-A, ETH-B, ETH-C, WSTETH-A, and WSTETH-B to zero and removing them from DC-IAM. data.title: STOCKS | Afterpay Co-Founder Nick Molnar to Leave Company and Block at Year-End
data.description:
Afterpay co-founder Nick Molnar said he will leave the company and its U.S. parent, Block, at the end of this year, saying he wants to spend more time with his family. According to Sina Finance, Molnar shared the news on LinkedIn on Saturday; he co-founded the Australian buy now, pay later company with Anthony Eisen in 2014.

Block, the payments fintech company led by Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey, acquired Afterpay for $29 billion in 2021. Dorsey has been restructuring Block with a focus on artificial intelligence and announced large-scale layoffs in February; Afterpay employees were reportedly also laid off.

Molnar said he was proud of what the company had done to take Australian technology overseas. He added that he was encouraged by Australian entrepreneurs following similar paths and looked forward to seeing more success stories like theirs on the global stage.

data.title: Nvidia Investor Liao Kaiyuan, With $1.3 Billion Stake, Backs Jensen Huang and Says He Won’t Invest More if Leadership Changes
data.description: Billionaire investor and Nvidia shareholder Liao Kaiyuan said Friday that he supports Jensen Huang. According to Odaily, Liao said by text message that he would make no further investment if Huang were no longer leading the company, and put his investment in Nvidia at about $1.3 billion.

data.title: Whale Adds to ZEC Long on Each Dip; 5x Position Shows $3.5 Million Loss
data.description: A whale holds a ZEC long position worth about $18.5 million, with an unrealized loss of about $3.5 million. According to Odaily, Hyperbot data shows the trader added to the 5x leveraged position as ZEC fell, buying near $1,170, $1,030, $970 and $904 yesterday morning, and adding funds to maintain the position during the decline. data.title: Nvidia Shareholders Urge Board to Assess Options, Including Jensen Huang’s Return
data.description:
Brad Gerstner, chief executive of Altimeter Capital Management, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, have jointly written to Nvidia’s board as shareholders. According to Odaily, they urged the board to use a deliberate process to consider the company’s future leadership and keep all options open, including Jensen Huang’s return.

The investors said questions about recent events outnumber answers and cautioned against rushing to choose a successor, arguing that would not serve shareholders’ interests. They said Nvidia could continue operating under Colette Kress and her team during the transition, and that the board had time to make the right decision. They added that deciding against Huang’s return after establishing the facts would be within the board’s authority, but said his record as the company’s founder and longtime leader warranted careful consideration before any replacement.
